1#main: The law of sewing a Sefer Torah. In it are 4 seifim. One sews a Sefer Torah only with sinews of a pure domestic animal or wild animal; and one should not sew the entire sheet from its head to its end, but rather leave a little at its head and a little at its end unsewn, and all the rest sewn from head to end; and one sews from the outside (Terumat HaDeshen siman 50).
2#main: One places in a Sefer Torah two poles—one at its head and one at its end—and what he left of margin at its head and end he wraps on the poles and sews them with sinews; and two fingerbreadths should remain between the pole and the page. (And in a time of pressure when it is impossible to sew it with sinews, if it was sewn with silk around the poles—they read from it; however, if it is possible to repair it with sinews, even though it was already sewn with silk, they do not read from it until it is repaired) (Terumat HaDeshen siman 51).
3#main: If the majority of the sewing between sheet and sheet was torn and they are still connected by five or six enduring stitches—it is valid (there, siman 50).
4#main: If one sheet is not sewn with it, even if it lies with it—they do not read from it.
